steps.label: A physical, two-state system
steps.sub: A voltage level, a magnetic domain, a punched hole — 0 or 1 is a human label on hardware

steps.label: Determinism
steps.sub: At any instant the bit is in exactly one state; unknown means unread, not undefined

steps.label: Exclusivity
steps.sub: One bit holds one value at a time — never a combination of both

steps.label: Non-disturbing readout
steps.sub: Reading or copying a bit never changes the original

steps.label: 1 bit = 2 states, 2 bits = 4 states
steps.sub: In general, n classical bits have 2ⁿ possible configurations

steps.label: 8 bits = 256 values, 32 bits > 4 billion
steps.sub: That exponential is real — it's why a byte and a 32-bit address work the way they do

steps.label: But 2ⁿ counts possibilities, not simultaneous states
steps.sub: It's the size of the space the system could visit, across every input

steps.label: At any instant, exactly one string is realized
steps.sub: An 8-bit register holds one definite value, like 01101010 — nothing else

steps.label: Classical bits occupy pure, definite, exclusive states
steps.sub: Any uncertainty is the observer's ignorance, not a physical property

steps.label: No mechanism for structured 'many possibilities at once'
steps.sub: Nothing in the classical model lets one system carry interfering possibilities

steps.label: That absence is the whole reason quantum computing exists
steps.sub: It's not just faster transistors — it's a different kind of object

steps.label: Next: the qubit, formally defined
steps.sub: A vector with internal structure that has no classical analog

subtitle: The real object behind a qubit: a state vector, not 'secretly both 0 and 1.'
